## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Articulation: how each note is played"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### Staccato
<p>Short and detached: a gap after each note. A dot over or under the notehead.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
.C .E .G .c|.G .E .C z|]
</script><script type="text/plain" data-bend>
{"bpm":100,"sound":"piano","notes":[{"t":0,"d":0.35,"midi":60},{"t":1,"d":0.35,"midi":64},{"t":2,"d":0.35,"midi":67},{"t":3,"d":0.35,"midi":72},{"t":4,"d":0.35,"midi":67},{"t":5,"d":0.35,"midi":64},{"t":6,"d":0.35,"midi":60}]}
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Legato
<p>Smooth, no gaps. A <strong>slur</strong> (a curve over <em>different</em> notes) asks for it.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
(C E G c|G E C) z|]
</script><script type="text/plain" data-bend>
{"bpm":100,"sound":"piano","notes":[{"t":0,"d":1.08,"midi":60},{"t":1,"d":1.08,"midi":64},{"t":2,"d":1.08,"midi":67},{"t":3,"d":1.08,"midi":72},{"t":4,"d":1.08,"midi":67},{"t":5,"d":1.08,"midi":64},{"t":6,"d":1,"midi":60}]}
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Slur or tie?
<p>A curve over different pitches is a <strong>slur</strong>: play them smoothly. A curve joining two of the <em>same</em> pitch is a <strong>tie</strong>: one note, held for both.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
(C E G) c-|c4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Accent
<p><code>&gt;</code>: a strong start to the note. Marks combine: a dot <em>and</em> an accent is short and strong.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
!>!G B d B|!>!.G .B !>!.d z|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Tenuto and marcato
<p><strong>Tenuto</strong> (a short line): hold the full length, with a little weight. <strong>Marcato</strong> (<code>^</code>): stronger than an accent.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="88"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
!tenuto!G !tenuto!B !tenuto!d2|!tenuto!c !tenuto!A G2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Glissando
<p>A slide from one note to another. Violin, trombone, voice: through every pitch. Piano, harp: a sweep across keys or strings.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="70"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
!slide!D A|]
</script><script type="text/plain" data-bend>
{"bpm":70,"sound":"violin","notes":[{"t":0,"d":3.6,"midi":62,"bend":[[0,0],[1.2,0],[2,7]]}]}
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Arco
<p>Strings, played with the bow (the normal way). Written <em>arco</em> after a pizzicato passage.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="violin" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:D
D F A d|A F D2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Pizzicato
<p><em>pizz.</em>: strings plucked with a finger instead of bowed.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="pizzicato_strings" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:D
D F A d|A F D2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Other techniques
<ul>
<li><strong>Double stopping</strong>: two strings at once</li>
<li><strong>Con sordino</strong>: with a mute (<em>senza sord.</em> takes it off)</li>
<li><strong>Tremolo</strong>: one note repeated very fast</li>
<li><strong>Vibrato</strong>: the pitch wavers a little, for warmth</li>
<li><strong>Falsetto</strong>: a light, high voice above the normal range</li>
</ul>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### How players slur
<ul>
<li><strong>Strings</strong>: many notes in one bow stroke</li>
<li><strong>Wind, brass</strong>: tongue only the first note</li>
<li><strong>Voice</strong>: one breath, the vowel kept going</li>
<li><strong>Piano</strong>: hold each key until the next is down</li>
</ul>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="articulation"></div>
:::::

## Describing articulation

- Name the mark and say what it does to the sound: "the strings play **pizzicato**, so the notes are short and light".
- Articulation is how a note is played, not how loud it is: that is [dynamics](elements-dynamics-sheet.qmd).

- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 1: Articulation](elements-articulation.qmd).
